# Review — PAN-5361
## Verdict: CHANGES REQUESTED — issue AC1 unmet on the PR's own calibration data: one +20 burst on one idle window flips 9 of 20 clean runs to FAIL

## Context
- Run ID: agent-pan-5361-review-fa257f60
- Manifest: /home/eltmon/Projects/overdeck/workspaces/feature-pan-5361/.pan/review/agent-pan-5361-review-fa257f60/context.json
- Branch / workspace: feature/pan-5361 / /home/eltmon/Projects/overdeck/workspaces/feature-pan-5361
- PR: https://github.com/eltmon/overdeck/pull/5373
- HEAD reviewed: fa257f6057c6ba28b171e45987d2e8cbdb621f72 (the dispatch SHA)
- Base / prior cycle SHA: merge-base 46b50b03500; no prior review cycle
- Note: during this review the work agent pushed 166a2edf800 ("keep every program's total until the cross-window merge", a CodeRabbit fix to the diagnostic `spawns.top` ranking plus one test). That commit touches only diagnostics and does not change the blocker below. It was not reviewed as part of this cycle.

## Blocking Findings

### [requirements] Min-of-3 does not make the Linux verdict robust to a single burst; the idle side is effectively min-of-2 because window 2 is the dashboard's own startup work — `scripts/bare-host-smoke.sh` (`take_windows`, `measure_idle`), `scripts/bare-host-smoke/result.mjs` (`decideIdle`)
- Severity: `!` (failure of an explicit in-scope acceptance criterion: issue AC1, the core goal of the issue)
- Classification / requirement scope: specification defect (FR-1 narrowed issue AC1 on a premise that the calibration falsifies), plus a validation gap (the unit tests and the CP-1 rule cannot detect it); in_pr_scope. The code follows FR-1 faithfully, so this is not an implementation bug in the arithmetic.
- Requirement text:
  - Issue AC1: "decide the Linux idle verdict on a measure that a single host burst of up to +65 PIDs in any one baseline or idle window cannot move above or below the budget."
  - PRD FR-1 weakened this to "only by the normal spread between that side's windows". The PRD's critique response justifies the weakening by calling the residual "the few-PID window spread, which the D14 budget (3 × the highest calibration net) already absorbs". The PRD's own "Unresolved after two critic rounds" list still contains "A single burst can flip the verdict".
- Trigger and changed-code connection: `take_windows idle` takes 3 back-to-back windows starting `SETTLE_SECS`=20 s after health. In 18 of 20 calibration runs (and in the live PR-head run), idle window 2 (about +52 s to +82 s after boot) holds a one-time burst of Overdeck dashboard work. The per-window `spawn-trace.log` for linux-01 shows window 1 `{ps:3, getconf:2, lsblk:1}`, window 2 `{ps:4, node:1, docker:4, git:2, jq:1, claude:2, herdr:4, sh:1, which:4, curl:1, getconf:2}` (26 traced calls, tree +6 tasks, 120–200 new PIDs) and window 3 `{ps:3, getconf:2}`. The two runs without that window-2 work (linux-03, linux-15) have window 2 at 24 and 22. So window 2 can never be the minimum, and `min(idle)` is in practice `min(w1, w3)`. Windows 1 and 3 differ by 13–45 PIDs (w1 is about 16–20 or about 44; w3 is about 28–35 or about 56–64). A burst on whichever of the two is lower moves the minimum to the other one, which is often over budget.
- Expected / observed / impact:
  - Expected (AC1): no single +65 burst on any one window can move the verdict across the budget.
  - Observed: I replayed the 20 plain calibration runs (artifacts of run 43734201237) and added a single burst to each idle window in turn, taking the worst case per run. The nets at budget 30:

    | burst on one idle window | runs flipped PASS→FAIL (of 20) |
    | --- | --- |
    | +20 | 9 (01, 04, 07, 09, 11, 16, 17, 19, 20) |
    | +30 | 12 |
    | +60 | 12 |

    Bursts on the baseline side are absorbed, as designed; the worst baseline +60 case moves no run toward failure. With the issue's per-window idle burst rate of about 7%, the expected flake rate stays at the same few-percent order as today's 3.3% (7 of 211).
  - Margin: five of the 20 clean runs already net 23–27 against a budget of 30. D14's "3 × highest" headroom does not apply, because `min(30, 3 × 27)` is capped at 30, so the margin is 3 PIDs. This is the margin the critique response said D14 would absorb.
  - Baseline comparison (this is not a regression): on the same 20 runs the old single-window rule (w1 minus baseline 1) would have failed 5 (01: 41, 04: 32, 07: 38, 09: 38, 19: 36), and linux-02 would have gone negative (−17). The new rule fails 0 of 20 and has no negative net. So the change is a real improvement over today, but it does not meet AC1. Twenty clean runs also prove little about a 3% failure mode: 0.97^20 ≈ 54%.
  - The PRD "Observation" and `docs/RELEASING.md` explain window 2 wrongly. The PRD calls it "a systematic effect tied to elapsed wall-clock time since runner boot". The trace shows it is the idle dashboard's own deferred startup work (a `node` child, `claude`, `herdr`, `docker`, `which`, `curl`), so it is not runner noise.
- Evidence: static trace of `take_windows`/`decideIdle`; per-window dump of all 24 Linux calibration `result.json` files and the linux-01 and linux-03 `spawn-trace.log` (downloaded to the review scratchpad); a burst-injection replay over the 20 plain runs (a node script reusing the `min(idle) − min(baseline)` arithmetic). Live PR-head run 43735818238 has the same shape: baseline 8,5,11; idle 19,201,32 (window 2 = 26 traced calls); net 14, PASS. Limit: the replay assumes bursts add to one window's count, as the issue's evidence describes; it does not model two bursts.
- Fix: correct the specification first, then the measure. Idle behaviour is out of bounds (non-goal 2), so the fix must change only the smoke's measure. Options, in the order I'd try them:
  1. Start the idle windows after the dashboard's one-time startup work. For example, raise the Linux-only settle time, or wait until the traced deferred-startup calls have stopped, before window 1. Then all 3 idle windows are steady state and min-of-3 gives the immunity FR-1 assumes.
  2. Or keep the timing and raise `WINDOWS_PER_SIDE_LINUX` so that at least 3 steady-state idle windows follow the startup burst.

  Then restore FR-1 to the issue's AC1 wording. Add a unit test built from a real calibration shape (for example linux-01: baseline 6,8,10 and idle 47,126,33 plus +20 on window 3 must still pass). Recalibrate, and record the burst-injection replay result (no flips for +20/+30/+65 on any single window) as calibration evidence. Fix the CP-1 rule too: its idle median (39) was inflated by the window-2 startup work, which is why it did not fire.

## Non-blocking Findings

- `~` [requirements/docs] **The PRD calibration table disagrees with its artifacts** (`.pan/drafts/pan-5361.md`, "Calibration evidence"). linux-02's deciding window is 0 in `result.json`, but the table says 2. The attribution column says "unattributed" for all 20 rows, but nine runs report `dashboard-tree` (02, 03, 05, 06, 10, 14, 15, 18, 20). The nets and window counts are correct. Regenerate the table from the artifacts.
- `~` [docs] The `docs/RELEASING.md` and smoke-header claim that min-of-3 "keeps one such burst from moving the net by more than the normal spread" is literally true, but it misleads: the real idle spread is 13–45 PIDs, which crosses the budget. Update it with the fix above.
- `?` [correctness, diagnostic only] Before 166a2edf800, per-window `top` was sliced to 10 before `mergeTop`, so a program split across windows could drop out of the merged top-10 (CodeRabbit thread 4579249320). It affects only the printed or JSON `spawns.top`, never the verdict or `cost`. The work agent has already pushed a fix; I did not review it.
- `?` [correctness, diagnostic only] FR-6 attribution uses 2 × slack, so 9 of 20 passing clean runs report `dashboard-tree`. That is harmless, because attribution prints only on failure, but it is biased toward blaming the dashboard (Decision 9 says this bias is intended).
- `?` [performance] `tree_snapshot` is an O(n²) fixpoint over every `/proc` entry in bash. That is fine at runner scale (about 200–300 processes). The live `bare-host-linux` job took 5m36s against 3m32s for main's last run (+2m04s, within the NFR-3 budget of about +3 min).

## Coverage

Changed-file ledger (reviewed at fa257f60):
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: reviewed. The canary job's `needs: [build, bare-host-changes]` and `if: needs.bare-host-changes.outputs.smoke == 'true'` match `bare-host-macos-known-bad`. The assertion step checks setupError, rc 1, panUp, enoent, rule, value > budget, injectedSpawnerMs 500 and attribution `dashboard-tree`. The artifact upload is `if: always()`. Both filters gained `scripts/bare-host-smoke/**`. No calibration workflow and no `strategy:` on `bare-host-linux`.
- `scripts/bare-host-smoke.sh`: reviewed. `SCRIPT_DIR` resolves before `cd`. `new_pids` is unchanged. `take_windows` stamps from/to and snapshots outside the counter reads (NFR-1), and a retake re-snapshots before its `from` stamp. macOS keeps `$(date +%s)000/999` inclusive bounds and N=1. `tree_snapshot` uses builtins only: no `$(`, backtick or pipe; `read -d ''` and `local -a` are bash 3.2-safe; the `/proc/<pid>/stat` field index (`$2` ppid, `${18}` num_threads after stripping "pid (comm) ") is correct; it is called only under `OS_NAME = linux`. `--idle-spawner-ms` rejects non-digits and values below 50 (64). The spawner preload has an `argv[1]` guard and loads after the tracer. The tracer gained a `shell` field.
- `scripts/bare-host-smoke/result.mjs`: reviewed. `decideIdle` handles empty idle windows (spawns null, value null, pass false). macOS traced-cost with one window is the same as the old inline program (inclusive `to`, same cost formula, same top ordering). The Linux half-open bounds are correct, and attribution follows FR-6 (max, not sum). The env parsing tolerates missing tree entries.
- `tests/unit/scripts/bare-host-smoke-result.test.ts`: reviewed (14 tests at fa257f60). It is under `tests/unit/**`, so the default vitest include runs it. The tests use synthetic idle windows with a 1–2 PID spread, which is why they cannot show the blocking finding.
- `docs/PIPELINE-GATES.md`, `docs/RELEASING.md`, `.overdeck/context/codebase/conventions.md`: reviewed. They state the min-of-3 measure, the calibration nets and the canary job. The wording issue is noted above.
- `.pan/drafts/pan-5361.md`, `.pan/drafts/pan-5361-critique*.md`, `.pan/specs/…xbrief.json`, `.pan/continues/PAN-5361.xbrief.json`: reviewed as requirements sources. The table inaccuracy is noted above.

Dimensions:
- Correctness: arithmetic, bounds, retake path, bash 3.2 compatibility and env contract are all traced; no implementation defect found. The blocker is in the measure design.
- Security: CI-only shell and Node code with no new trust boundary. The `/proc` reads are local and read-only. The spawner preload runs only under `--idle-spawner-ms` and spawns a fixed `true`. Nothing found.
- Performance: the snapshot cost and the job-duration delta are within NFR-3.
- Requirements/UX: see the AC matrix.

Acceptance criteria (issue ACs, then PRD AC-WIn):

| AC-WI1 | met | 14 tests in the named groups; `bash -n` OK; `write_result` has no `node -e`; CI test shards green on fa257f60 |

| AC-WI4 | met | Value check rejects < 50 (64); canary job, needs and if as specified; both filters updated |

## Verification
- `gh pr checks 5373` / run 43735818238 (headSha fa257f60): `bare-host-linux` success (net 14), `bare-host-linux-spawner-canary` success (net 64, FAIL detected, `dashboard-tree`), `bare-host-macos` success, `bare-host-macos-known-bad` success, test-shard 1–4 success, lint-group (core/effect/skills/state) success, `overdeck/test` verification gate passed. These are the exact-HEAD results I cite for tests and for effect diagnostics (`lint-group (effect)`).
- `bash -n scripts/bare-host-smoke.sh`: OK. Grep for bash-4-only constructs: none.
- `npx vitest run tests/unit/scripts/bare-host-smoke-result.test.ts`: 15 passed. This ran against the work agent's uncommitted edits (later pushed as 166a2edf800), so it is not evidence for fa257f60; the CI shards above are.

### [requirements] Min-of-3 does not make the Linux verdict robust to a single burst; the idle side is effectively min-of-2 — `scripts/bare-host-smoke.sh` (`take_windows`, `measure_idle`), `scripts/bare-host-smoke/result.mjs` (`decideIdle`)

- Classification / requirement scope: a specification defect. FR-1 narrowed issue AC1 on the premise that the residual is a "few-PID window spread". The PR's own calibration falsifies that premise. There is also a validation gap: the unit tests use 1–2 PID spreads. Scope: in_pr_scope. Carried over unchanged from cycle fa257f60.
- Trigger and changed-code connection: idle window 2 (about +52 s to +82 s after boot) holds a one-time burst of dashboard startup work in 18 of 20 calibration runs and in both live PR-head runs. In linux-01, `spawn-trace.log` shows window 2 making `node`, `claude`, `herdr`, `docker`, `which`, `curl` and `git` calls: 26 traced calls and 120–200 new PIDs. Window 2 is therefore never the minimum, so `min(idle)` reduces to `min(w1, w3)`. Windows 1 and 3 differ by 13–45 PIDs. A burst on the lower of the two moves the minimum to the other one, which is often above the budget.
- Expected / observed / impact: I replayed the 20 plain calibration runs (artifacts of run 43734201237) with a single burst added to each idle window in turn. A +20 burst flips 9 of 20 runs to FAIL. A +30 or +60 burst flips 12 of 20. Five clean runs already net 23–27 against the budget of 30. The D14 rule gives no headroom here because it is capped at 30. The change still improves on the old rule, which fails 5 of the same 20 runs, but issue AC1 requires that a single burst of up to +65 cannot cross the budget.
- Evidence: see the prior report for the per-window dumps, the trace breakdown and the replay table. The re-check at 8f9a2499 found the measure code byte-identical to fa257f60: `git diff fa257f60 8f9a2499 -- scripts/bare-host-smoke.sh` is empty, and the `result.mjs` diff only removes a `.slice(0, 10)` in `summarizeSpawns`.
- Fix (unchanged): change only the measure, because non-goal 2 forbids changing idle behaviour.
  1. Start the Linux idle windows after the dashboard's one-time startup work. One way is a longer Linux-only settle time. Another is to wait until the deferred startup calls stop.
  2. Or add enough windows that at least 3 steady-state windows follow the startup burst.
  3. Restore FR-1 to the issue's AC1 wording.
  4. Add a unit test built from a real calibration shape. Example: linux-01, baseline 6,8,10, idle 47,126,33, plus +20 on window 3, must still pass.

The table also marks 9 runs as unattributed that the artifacts report as `dashboard-tree` (02, 03, 05, 06, 10, 14, 15, 18, 20). Separately, the PRD "Observation" calls window 2 runner-boot noise, but the trace shows it is dashboard startup work. Carried over.
